stem:
Globally, measles is an important disease that mainly affects children. Many deaths from measles occur in children under five years of age.

Table 3.1 shows the population of six countries in Africa in 2009 and the number of cases of measles per 100 000 people for the four years 2009 to 2012.

All six countries are classified as low-income countries.

{{figure:reviewed_table_1.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
The actual number of cases of measles in Chad in 2009 was 165 and in Eritrea was 82.

Calculate the actual number of cases of measles in Ethiopia in 2009.

Show your working.

{{figure:reviewed_response_1.png}}

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data for Chad, Eritrea and Ethiopia to explain the advantages of showing the data in Table 3.1 as number of cases of measles per 100 000 people rather than the actual number of cases.

{{figure:reviewed_response_2.png}}

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Fig. 3.1 shows the percentage of children vaccinated against measles over a ten year period from 2003 to 2012.

• The percentage vaccinated represents children under one year of age who have been given at least one dose of the vaccine against measles in the given year.
• The data are for the six African countries shown in Table 3.1.

{{figure:figure-3-1-full-v2.webp}}
parts.text:
Vaccination is known to protect populations against infectious diseases.

Some of the data in Table 3.1 (on page 4) and Fig. 3.1 (on page 6) support this statement.

Describe the data that support this statement and comment on the data that do not support this statement.

{{figure:reviewed_response_3.png}}
